children: has won a nearly $140 million US government contract to upgrade communications equipment at 63 federal prison facilities over the next two years, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing the company and the Federal Bureau of Prisons.

The project involves replacing aging radios and dispatch consoles, with the bureau planning to distribute 22,000 new radios. The devices will include some access to cellular networks and a feature that triggers an emergency alert if a corrections officer falls.
The upgrades aim to improve communications and staff safety across the bureau’s facilities. Motorola
Chief Operating Officer Jack Molloy said the new equipment would help officers stay connected in areas with thick prison walls and cellular dead zones.
Bureau Director William K. Marshall III described the modernization as an investment in staff safety and institutional security.
The bureau employs more than 34,000 people, operates 118 institutions, and manages an inmate population of more than 150,000.
A bureau spokesperson told Bloomberg that the project complies with the Prison Camera Reform Act of 2021 and will be funded through allocations under last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
The contract also includes upgrades at two sites that manage radio traffic and monitor the communications network.

title: Motorola secures $140M deal to modernize federal prison radios
